## Minneapolis bar-service shortlist

| Business | City | Why it fits | Full-service? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Surdyk’s Catering** | Minneapolis | Wine, beer, spirits, and Sidebar-originated signature cocktails; food catering too. | **Yes — especially strong.** Menu planning, staffing, rentals, cocktail-style receptions, antipasti/hors d’oeuvres, and buffet dinners. |
| **Mintahoe Catering & Events** | Minneapolis | Explicit **bar & beverage service** alongside customized food menus. | **Yes.** Markets “seamless full-service” for meals and bar service. |
| **D’Amico Hospitality** | Minneapolis | Dedicated beverage/bar-service menus plus chef-curated food, receptions, stations, pastry, and venues. | **Yes.** A good all-in-one choice for a larger or polished party. |
| **Chowgirls Catering** | Minneapolis | Food caterer that specifically advertises “stylish solutions for all your bar needs.” | **Likely full-service.** Worth asking for holiday bar packages, staffing, and rentals. |
| **LiquidMotion Insured Bartending Service** | Minneapolis area | Bar-focused caterer; reviews specifically reference signature drinks and event planning. | **Bar-service specialist** rather than food caterer. |
| **Bootleg Blondie Mobile Bar** | Minneapolis | Mobile bar; event reviews mention tailored menus and larger team events. | Bar-focused; good for a custom cocktail setup. |
| **Agave MPLS** | Minneapolis | Mobile bartending team; reviews cite cocktails and a holiday-party booking. | Bar-focused. |
| **Minnybar Mobile Beverage** | Minneapolis area | Mobile beverage/camper-bar service; corporate-event experience. | Bar-focused. |
| **Piccadilly Pours** | Minneapolis area | Mobile bar/tap-wall option; reviews mention custom drink menus, cocktails, and mocktails. | Bar-focused; nice fit if you want a visible mocktail component. |

**Best “one vendor handles it” calls:** Surdyk’s, Mintahoe, D’Amico, then Chowgirls. Confirm alcohol-purchasing/licensing rules, bartender count, glassware/ice, setup/teardown, and whether they can serve at your specific venue.

### Surdyk’s: what it actually offers
- **Food:** drop-off or full-service catering; antipasti stations, inventive hors d’oeuvres, and buffet dinners.
- **Beverage:** expert-selected **wine, beer, and spirits**, plus **signature cocktails** from Sidebar at Surdyk’s.
- **Event support:** menu planning, staffing, and rentals.  
**Location:** 2117 West River Road N., Minneapolis. This is clearly a full-service contender.

## Nonalcoholic Instant Pot mulligatawny
Adapted from Simply Happy Foodie’s pressure-cooker recipe; make it vegetarian/nonalcoholic by omitting chicken and using vegetable broth.

**Ingredients (4–6 servings)**
- 2 Tbsp olive oil; 4 Tbsp butter (or more oil)
- 1 diced onion, 3 diced celery stalks, 2 diced carrots, ½ diced green bell pepper
- 3 minced garlic cloves; 2 tsp grated ginger
- 1½ Tbsp curry powder; 1½ tsp garam masala
- ¼ tsp each nutmeg, cinnamon, thyme, black pepper; ½ tsp salt
- 6 cups **vegetable broth**
- 1 drained 15-oz can diced tomatoes
- ½ cup rinsed white rice; 1 diced apple; 3 whole cloves
- 1 cup coconut milk; ¼ cup flour

**Simple steps**
1. Sauté onion, celery, carrots, pepper in oil/butter until beginning to soften. Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute; stir in spices.
2. Add broth, tomatoes, rice, apple, and cloves. Pressure-cook **7 minutes**, then natural-release **20 minutes**.
3. Switch back to sauté. Whisk flour into coconut milk, stir it in, and simmer until lightly thickened. Remove whole cloves; salt to taste.

It is naturally alcohol-free and easily vegan if you use oil instead of butter.
